Since `j - i >= 1`, `(j-i)/2 < j-i` (because `(j-i)/2 <= (j-i)/2 < j-i` for `j-i >= 1`... actually for `j-i = 1`, `(1)/2 = 0 < 1` ✓; for `j-i = 2`, `(2)/2 = 1 < 2` ✓). For the other recursive call `SearchRecursive(a,m+1,j,x)`, the decreases is `j-(m+1) = j-m-1`. We need `j-m-1 < j-i`, i.e., `m+1 > i`, i.e., `m >= i`. Since `m = i + (j-i)/2 >= i` (because `(j-i)/2 >= 0` when `j > i`), this holds. And we need `j-m-1 >= 0`, i.e., `m+1 <= j`, i.e., `m < j`. Since `m = i + (j-i)/2 < i + (j-i) = j` when `j-i > 0` (because `(j-i)/2 < j-i` for `j-i >= 1`), this holds.

So the decreases SHOULD work if we have `0 <= i <= j <= |a|` as a precondition. The problem is that this precondition is MISSING from `SearchRecursive`.

1. The requires `forall p, q :: i <= p < q < j ==> a[p] >= a[q]` is now well-formed because `i <= p` and `q < j <= |a|` ensures `0 <= p < |a|` and `0 <= q < |a|`.

4. For `SearchRecursive(a,m+1,j,x)`: needs `0 <= m+1 <= j <= |a|`. We have `m >= i >= 0` so `m+1 >= 1 > 0`. And `m < j` so `m+1 <= j`. And `j <= |a|`. ✓

6. Decreases for recursive call 2: `j-(m+1) < j-i`. Since `m >= i`, `j-(m+1) <= j-(i+1) = j-i-1 < j-i`. And `j-(m+1) >= 0` since `m+1 <= j`. ✓

So the fix is to add `requires 0 <= i <= j <= |a|;` to `SearchRecursive`.
